title: Separable and purely inseparable extensions are linearly disjoint
statement: Let $k\subseteq K$ and $k\subseteq L$ be field extensions [def-pc-field-extension] embedded in a common field $\Omega$. Assume that $K/k$ is separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and that $L/k$ is purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Then the canonical $K$-algebra map $K\otimes_kL\to KL\subseteq\Omega$, $x\otimes y\mapsto xy$, is injective; equivalently, $K$ and $L$ are linearly disjoint over $k$.

source.place: Fields, Definition Tag 09IF (fields-definition-linearly-disjoint), in Section Tag 09IC (fields-section-linearly-disjoint), defines linear disjointness as injectivity of K ⊗_k L → KL; the statement itself is not a lemma of the Stacks project (Tag 030K = fields-lemma-separable-first is the decomposition E/E_sep/F of an algebraic extension, and Tag 07QH = algebra-lemma-geometrically-regular-over-separable-algebraic is unrelated). The statement is Mathlib's IntermediateField.linearDisjoint_of_isPurelyInseparable_of_isSeparable (Mathlib/FieldTheory/PurelyInseparable/Tower.lean:99).

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: take Mathlib's (F, E, K, S) = (k, L, Ω, K) with K an intermediate field of Ω/k, Algebra.IsSeparable k K (def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension) and IsPurelyInseparable k L (def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension, no finiteness needed); the conclusion K.LinearDisjoint L is by definition (FieldTheory/LinearDisjoint.lean:157, RingTheory/LinearDisjoint.lean:155) Subalgebra.LinearDisjoint of K and the image of L, which Subalgebra.linearDisjoint_iff_injective (RingTheory/LinearDisjoint.lean:232) turns into injectivity of Subalgebra.mulMap : K ⊗_k L → Ω, x ⊗ y ↦ xy; injectivity into Ω is injectivity into KL since the image lies in KL

split_report.summary: Checked the cited tags: Fields 030K is fields-lemma-separable-first (separable/purely-inseparable decomposition of an algebraic extension) and Algebra 07QH is about geometric regularity over separable algebraic extensions; neither proves this statement, and the Stacks project contains no lemma that does (fields.tex only defines linear disjointness, Definition 09IF in Section 09IC). Source corrected to 09IF plus the Mathlib declaration. Mathlib states exactly this, for arbitrary (possibly infinite) separable algebraic K/k and purely inseparable L/k inside Ω: IntermediateField.linearDisjoint_of_isPurelyInseparable_of_isSeparable (Tower.lean:99), whose conclusion unfolds to injectivity of K ⊗_k L → Ω. Status set to mathlib with the match; no proof steps and no new nodes. The definition node def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension defines both purely inseparable and finite purely inseparable extensions, so the statement's general hypothesis is covered; the citer lem-weil-pbc-separable-tensor-purely-inseparable-field uses only the finite case. Statement and stmt_deps kept.
